key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN models can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify safe process windows that reduce defects.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports faster parameter selection for robust thermoplastic welding by linking process settings, temperature, force, and defect formation into an actionable design map.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW
Experimental validation across rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating conditions
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained to predict temperature and axial force responses
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong agreement with experiments (R2 = 0.91 to 0.99), and the CEL model matched void formation plus thermal and mechanical responses, including force reduction from about 1600 N to 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: The process map is based on a specific HDPE setup and parameter range, so broader use may require retraining and revalidation for different materials, thicknesses, or tool geometries.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
